clue.text: Thumping music producing some discomfort

indicators.note: some of a word is only part of it, so the letters sit inside discomfort

explanation.surface: Loud, pounding music is causing a listener some unease.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a style of dance music with a heavy, pounding beat.

clue.text: Confusion over front for book jacket

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another sits above it in the grid

parts.note: a dust, as in a dust-up, is a commotion or row
a front for something illegal is a cover for it

explanation.surface: Muddle over what goes on the front of a book's wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust cover is the removable paper wrapper protecting a hardback.

clue.text: Lift most of the secrecy

parts.note: to lift is slang for to steal

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but one letter, here dropping the last letter of the

explanation.surface: Raising the bulk of the hidden material.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting covertly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Labourer wasting time in tanker

indicators.note: wasting time means losing it, so the time letter is lost from the labourer word

parts.note: a toiler is someone who labours

explanation.surface: A worker idling away the hours aboard an oil tanker.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil, such as a naval refuelling vessel.

clue.text: Uninhibited castaway

definitions.meaning: left behind and deserted, like someone marooned

explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned behaviour lacks restraint, and something cast away has been left deserted.

clue.text: Curtail a chance to make a deal

parts.note: bridge is a card game in which each player takes a turn to deal the cards

explanation.surface: Cut short a card-player's opportunity to hand out the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to shorten a text, cutting it down.

clue.text: Craftsman Lord Finchley should have employed

definitions.text: Craftsman Lord Finchley should have employed

parts.words: Craftsman Lord Finchley should have employed
parts.note: Belloc's verse Lord Finchley tells of a lord killed mending his own electric light, ending that the wealthy should give employment to a skilled tradesman

explanation.surface: A tradesman whom a certain lord ought to have hired.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc's cautionary verse has Lord Finchley electrocuted while fixing a light himself; its moral is that the rich should employ a skilled worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a tradesman who makes or mends things.

clue.text: Discourage sap in fix

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
to sap or mine is to dig under a fortification

explanation.surface: Putting someone off drawing tree juice while in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a date or price is to settle or decide it.

clue.text: Old men in trouble finally hire someone to act for them

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of hire

explanation.surface: Elderly men in difficulty eventually hire an agent to represent them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is fodder: OMENIN is rearranged to NOMINE, then 'finally' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person appointed to act or stand on another's behalf.

clue.text: Slip into gear

definitions.meaning: to put clothes on, get changed

explanation.definitionFit: To dress is to put on clothes, and clothing in general is also called dress.

clue.text: Suspect trickery when real malts are far from smooth

indicators.note: letters that are far from smooth are rough and jumbled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker grows suspicious when genuine whiskies taste harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense that something is wrong is the idiom of sniffing out a rat.

clue.text: Member occupying tee in beautiful valley

indicators.note: one thing occupying another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician standing on a golf tee in a lovely vale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a famously scenic gorge in Thessaly, Greece.

clue.text: Jumps on sort of beetle in American resort

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the Colorado beetle is a pest of potato crops
springs means jumps

explanation.surface: Leaping onto a particular beetle while on holiday in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a city and resort at the foot of Pikes Peak.

clue.text: Sulky medium

definitions.meaning: a means by which something is expressed or conveyed

explanation.definitionFit: A sulky is a horse-drawn conveyance, and a vehicle for ideas is a medium.

clue.text: Study suitable end for service, or a prayer

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
fit means suitable

indicators.note: the end for a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Learning what fits the close of a church service, or a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Confiteor is the Latin prayer of confession said at Mass.

clue.text: Befuddled native taking drug in innocence

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside
befuddled means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A muddled local on drugs is in a state of innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Befuddled' rearranges NATIVE as NAIVTE, and 'taking' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is lack of worldly experience, a guileless simplicity.

clue.text: All are really stiff after beginning to exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces come after the first one
the beginning to a word is its first letter

parts.note: very means really
a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body

explanation.surface: Everyone is truly rigid after starting a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody means every person, the whole lot.

clue.text: Train held up for cortege

definitions.meaning: a train of followers attending someone
a procession or body of attendants

explanation.walkthrough: 'held up for' is a link here, not a reversal; both outer words define.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants, which a train or cortege also is.

clue.text: Where the teddy bears' dance is held?

definitions.text: Where the teddy bears' dance is held?

parts.words: Where the teddy bears' dance is held?
parts.note: a dance is a hop, and stuffed bears are playthings, so the venue is a shop full of them

explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling playthings is where teddy bears would be found.

clue.text: Right not advertised to the general public

definitions.text: not advertised to the general public
definitions.meaning: of medicines available only on prescription and promoted only to doctors

explanation.definitionFit: Ethical means morally sound; ethical drugs are prescription medicines not advertised to consumers.

clue.text: Branched flower-holder, not a pea-green reproduction

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy remade, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A forked vase that is not a copy in a bright green shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' means the A is taken out of PEAGREEN, and 'reproduction' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental table centrepiece with branching holders for fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Pendant with just a little spike at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece at the top comes first

parts.note: an ear is the spike of grain on a cereal plant
a drop is just a small amount

explanation.surface: A hanging jewel with a small point on top.
explanation.definitionFit: An eardrop is an earring that hangs down from the lobe.

clue.text: Opponents in class shown hand-held missile

indicators.note: the opponents are said to be in the class, so their letters go inside the class word

parts.note: a grade is a class or rank
in bridge East and North play against each other, so E and N are opponents

explanation.surface: Rivals in a classroom brandish a projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand.

clue.text: A shameless swindle, as shoplifting usually is

definitions.meaning: a blatant rip-off, especially an outrageous price
theft carried out during opening hours when it is light

explanation.definitionFit: Daylight robbery is the idiom for blatant overcharging, and literally theft done in the light of day.

clue.text: Fall out of love and languish

indicators.note: the fall word lies outside the love letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: to drop is to fall
O is love, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Falling out of love and pining away.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or flag, losing vigour.

clue.text: Bust shattered

explanation.definitionFit: Broke means penniless, and also smashed, as in broken.

clue.text: The colour is right in the line of fire for darts

indicators.note: right is said to be in the line, so its letter sits inside the darts word

parts.words: the line of fire for darts
parts.note: the oche is the line behind which a darts player stands to throw

explanation.surface: A shade that sits squarely where darts are thrown from.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the throwing line in darts, a pub game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment and that colour.

clue.text: Meat grilled a sort of black ends in trouble

indicators.note: the first piece ends in the second, which follows it

parts.note: carbon black is a pigment, and carbon a sooty black
ado is trouble or fuss

explanation.surface: Grilled meat that ends up burnt black and troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbonado is a piece of meat scored and broiled over coals.

clue.text: It helps to tie up loose ends in the office

definitions.text: It helps to tie up loose ends in the office

parts.words: It helps to tie up loose ends in the office
parts.note: sounds like finishing outstanding tasks at work, but literally a bent wire holding loose sheets together

explanation.definitionFit: A paperclip is a looped wire that holds loose sheets of paper together.

clue.text: Sort of paper that gives only rough coverage

definitions.text: Sort of paper that gives only rough coverage

parts.words: Sort of paper that gives only rough coverage
parts.note: sounds like a sloppy news report, but means abrasive paper whose coating is gritty

explanation.definitionFit: Emery paper is coated with abrasive grit, so its surface is rough.
